Have some film theory:

Split Edits:
Split Edits are a film editing technique where audio and video tracks are manipulated separately. In a L-cut, the audio from one scene continues into the next scene, while in a J-cut, the audio from the upcoming scene starts before the video changes. This technique enhances storytelling by creating smoother transitions and maintaining narrative flow.

Noddy Shots:
Noddy Shots refer to brief clips of a character nodding or reacting during conversations. These shots help convey engagement and can enhance dialogue scenes by showing emotional responses or reactions, making interactions feel more dynamic and realistic.

comments.text:
Notebooklm video summary

## Notebook LM: New Features and Future Implications

The video discusses Google's Notebook LM and its new features, focusing on the tool's potential to revolutionize content creation and consumption.

*Notebook LM is an AI-powered tool that helps users analyze and understand information.* It originally functioned as a text-based tool but now includes an audio overview feature that generates podcast-style summaries of uploaded documents.

*Key New Features:*

* *Customizable Podcasts:* Users can now direct the AI hosts to focus on specific sources, topics, and audiences.
* *Multitasking Mode:* Users can take notes while listening to the audio overview without interrupting the playback.
* *Business Edition:* A version specifically designed for companies with larger teams and more complex needs is in development.

*Impact on Content Creation:*

* The developers of Notebook LM see it as a new content medium rather than just a tool for mass production. 
* *Personalized Content:* The tool allows users to create content tailored to their specific needs, blurring the line between content creators and consumers.
* *Shift in Perspective:* Notebook LM encourages users to think of themselves as both creators and consumers of content. 

*Examples of Notebook LM Use Cases:*

* *Analyzing research documents and generating audio summaries.*
* *Summarizing meeting notes from lengthy group chats.*
* *Creating audio overviews of resumes and LinkedIn profiles.*
* *Turning a document filled with the words "poop" and "fart" into a 99-minute podcast.* This surprising example highlights the tool's ability to find meaning and generate engaging content even from seemingly nonsensical material. 

*Potential Future Implications:*

* *Increased Accessibility of Video Content:* Notebook LM's ability to generate audio and potentially video content could make it much easier and cheaper to produce high-quality content.
* *New Media Format:*  The personalized nature of AI-generated content could lead to a new form of media consumption.
* *Disruption of Traditional Media:* AI-powered tools like Notebook LM could challenge the existing models of news and information distribution.

*Ethical and Legal Considerations:*

* *Copyright Concerns:* The use of AI to summarize and present information from existing sources raises questions about copyright infringement.
* *Job Displacement:*  The increasing accessibility of AI content creation tools may lead to job losses in traditional media industries.

*The video concludes by urging viewers to embrace the potential of AI while remaining aware of its potential impact on society.* It emphasizes the importance of critical thinking and open-mindedness in navigating the evolving landscape of AI-generated content.

comments.text:
Maybe you should mention what you — ostensibly, because 99% of users don’t really know it — have already agreed to Google doing with those sources you upload…? You know, since you take the trouble to show us how easy it is to do and all. 

Advertisers must be very happy. Never before have they had access to technology that can read people’s individual diaries, observe their behavior as consumers and in private, and even experiment with different marketing to determine how to maximize the effectiveness of their manipulation. This means marketing well becomes the number one criterion for succeeding in any line of business, as opposed to providing the best product or service. 

And no, its not free. Ordinary people get the bill for all the costs, plus the profits, or else there isn’t a viable business. So I might not have to pay to watch this video, but whether I do or not, I’ll pay here, there and everywhere, for this “free” video and platform and all of the other “dree” stuff that has eradicated the market for real journalism, controversial and difficult topics, or outright depressing trends in society like this very phenomenon . 

I wonder what the world would have looked like today if Google had been able to succeed with a micropayment model instead of an advertising model. I don’t see how they could have, really, but I did blog about this stuff twenty years ago so the idea was definitely known well before search was monetized and the stage was set for the post-truth era we now find ourselves in. Marketing would be no more powerful than it used to, and more of the money would therefore be spent on making better products instead, and without issues like getting demonetized (and therefore also ignored by the almighty algorithm), so we’d have better products. And since our payments would actually depend on our use we might consume a bit less. There wouldn’t be a gazillion web sites designed to make you scroll for miles to maximize ad impressions before you finally learn how to enable the smart clipboard feature on Windows, but hundreds that gave the easiest to understand solutions the editor can muster — since we’d pay for the page view, the info we were after, and NOT ads. We would have our privacy still, and only government intelligence agencies would have much incentive to breach it. 

I don’t see how they could have done it back then. But I’m not so sure they can’t  now. They are making close to a billion dollars PER DAY in profits by being the world’s most advanced advertising agency (https://www.google.com/search?q=alphabet+finanials). 

But even to save the world, from the mess they are more responsible than anyone else for creating, they wouldn’t do that. Precisely because the billions are flowing in every day, and reinventing the entire business model means risking all that, in fact means it’s very unlikely they would end up on top again.
